sources.retainingWall.sliding: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.16 (p. 802) and Sec 3.14 (p. 801): 1.5 against sliding
sources.retainingWall.overturning: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.16 (p. 802) and Sec 3.14 (p. 800): 1.5 against overturning
sources.retainingWall.seismic: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.14 and 3.16 (pp. 800-802): 1.5, no reduction with earthquake
sources.retainingWall.passive: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.14(i) (p. 801): passive resistance is not counted where the abutting soil could be removed by excavation; counted in full only where the wall states that it cannot
sources.retainingWall.flotation: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.9.2(a)(iii) (p. 727): 0.9 x Dead Load + Buoyancy Pressure, i.e. 0.9 W >= U
sources.retainingWall.baseFriction: SAEngine practice, not BNBC: tan(r φ'), used only when the pack gives no friction coefficient
sources.retainingWall.adhesion: SAEngine practice, not BNBC: used only when the pack gives no friction coefficient
sources.retainingWall.yieldingKh: SAEngine practice, not BNBC (AASHTO LRFD 11.6.5.2.2: kh = 0.5 kh0 for a wall free to move 25-50 mm)
sources.strutAndTie: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Secs I.1-I.5 (part 2 pp. 481-495) and Sec 6.1.4.4 (p. 892); φ = 0.75 in Sec 6.2.3.2.6 (p. 898); deep beams by Appendix I, Sec 6.3.7.1 and 6.4.6; tieArm is SAEngine practice, not BNBC
sources.retainingWall.frictionCoefficient: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.14(iii) (p. 801): friction factor 0.5; a greater value only if verified by analysis and test
sources.shallow.bearingCombinations: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.9.2(a) (p. 727); Normal Live Load reduced as in column design (Sec 2.3.13)
sources.shallow.lateralIncrease: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.9.3 and 3.9.3.2 (p. 728): 33% with wind or earthquake, none for gravity loads alone
sources.shallow.factorOfSafety: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.9.3 (p. 728): 2.0 to 3.0 on the bearing capacity
sources.shallow.kern: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.9.1 (p. 727): resultant preferably within B/6 of the centre
sources.shallow.sliding: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.14 (p. 801): 1.5 against sliding; (i) no passive where the soil could be removed; (ii) no base friction under pile-supported structures
sources.shallow.minDepth: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.8.2(d) (p. 723): 500 mm below natural ground level unless rock or other weather resistant material is at the surface
sources.shallow.exteriorDepth: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.8.6 (p. 725): exterior footings of permanent structures 1.5 m in cohesive and 2 m in cohesionless soil, 400 mm for temporary ones; more on expansive soil
sources.shallow.raftDepth: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.8.10 (p. 726): 1.5 m in cohesive and 2 m in cohesionless soil
sources.shallow.slopeDistance: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.8.2 and 3.18 (pp. 724, 806): twice the footing width
sources.shallow.spreadAngle: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.8.2 (p. 723): masonry 1/2, lime concrete 2/3, cement concrete 1 horizontal to 1 vertical (fractions read on the PDF page)
sources.shallow.stepLap: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.8.2 and 3.18 (pp. 724, 806): the thickness of the foundation or three times the step height, whichever is greater
sources.shallow.minThickness: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.8.3 (p. 724) and Sec 6.8.7 (p. 978): RC 150 mm above the bottom bars on soil, 300 mm on piles; plain concrete 200 mm; masonry 250 mm
sources.shallow.presumptive: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.9.3.1 and Table 6.3.7 (pp. 728-729): two storeys or less in occupancy A-D, or the preliminary design of any structure
sources.shallow.subgrade: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.9.6.3 and Tables 6.3.9a-b (pp. 736-737): 300 mm plate, preliminary design
sources.shallow.settlementLimits: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.9.4.7(d) and Table 6.3.8 (pp. 732-733), a guide
sources.shallow.settlementGuide: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.9.4.7(d) (p. 732): isolated pad footings
sources.piles.staticMethod: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Secs 3.10.1.11-3.10.1.15 (pp. 743-748) for driven piles; Secs 3.10.4.3-3.10.4.6 (pp. 761-762) for bored piles: 2/3 of fs and 1/3 of fb; Sec 3.10.6.7 (pp. 772-775) for drilled shafts
sources.piles.soilClasses: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.3.9a (p. 736): sand loose N < 10, medium 10-30, dense 30 and over; Table 6.3.9b (p. 737): stiff clay from qu 100 kPa (cu 50). mediumCu 25 kPa (qu 50) is SAEngine practice, not BNBC (BNBC gives no soft / medium stiff bound)
sources.piles.static.alpha: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.1.12 Eq 6.3.16 (p. 745): α 1.0 for cu <= 25, 0.5 for cu >= 70, 1 - (cu - 25)/70 between. Note: the printed divisor 70 gives 0.36 at cu = 70, not 0.5 (a divisor of 90 would meet); the printed form is the more conservative and is used
sources.piles.static.sandBeta: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.1.14 Eq 6.3.23 (p. 747): β 0.10 at φ 33°, 0.20 at 35°, 0.35 at 37°; interpolated, the end values outside 33-37° (BNBC prints no others)
sources.piles.static.nq: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Fig 6.3.2 (p. 746, after Berezantzev et al. 1961), digitised from the PDF at 1° steps
sources.piles.static.nqDensity: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.1.14 Eq 6.3.24 (p. 748): Nq 8-12 loose, 12-40 medium, 40 dense sand; σ'v at the base at most 240 kPa. The engine takes the lesser of this range (interpolated in N60) and Fig 6.3.2 at the layer's φ
sources.piles.static.criticalDepth: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.1.15 (p. 748) and Sec 3.10.4.6 (p. 762): Dc = 10 D loose, 15 D medium dense, 20 D dense sand
sources.piles.static.boredSkin: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Secs 3.10.4.4 and 3.10.4.6 (p. 762): bored piles 2/3 of the driven fs and 1/3 of the driven fb
sources.piles.drilledShaft.minDiameter: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.6 (p. 770): bored piles of more than 600 mm are drilled shafts
sources.piles.drilledShaft.alpha: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.6.7 Eq 6.3.42 (p. 772): α 0.55 for su <= 190 kPa; above, Fig 6.3.3 (after Kulhawy and Jackson 1989) digitised from the PDF. Note: the figure's curve gives about 0.36 at 190 kPa, so α drops there as printed
sources.piles.drilledShaft.sideTop: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.6.7 (p. 773): no skin friction over the top 1.5 m and the bottom one diameter of a straight shaft
sources.piles.drilledShaft.clayReduceAbove: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Eqs 6.3.44a-d (p. 773): for Db > 1900 mm, fb' = Fr fb, Fr = 2.5 / (120 ω1 Db/Br + ω2) <= 1, ω1 = 0.0071 + 0.0021 L/Db <= 0.0015, ω2 = 1.59 √(Su/σr), 0.5 <= ω2 <= 1.5, Br 300 mm, σr 100 kPa. Note: as printed, ω1 is always 0.0015 (its first term already exceeds the limit); used as printed
sources.piles.drilledShaft.betaMax: SAEngine practice, not BNBC: β <= 1.2, β × N60/15 below N60 15 and fs <= 192 kPa (O'Neill and Reese 1999); conservative, kept and labelled. β is not floored (BNBC gives no lower bound; it is taken as at least 0)
sources.piles.drilledShaft.sandBase: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Eq 6.3.48 (p. 775): fb = 0.60 σr N60 <= 4500 kPa, N60 the mean from the base to 2 Db below; Eq 6.3.49: Fr = 4.17 Br/Db <= 1 for Db > 1200 mm
sources.piles.drilledShaft.lateralRatio: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.3.15 (p. 774), with Eq 6.3.46 β = K tan δ and Eq 6.3.19b K0 = (1 - sin φ') √OCR
sources.piles.drilledShaft.zetaLow: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.6.13 (p. 777): ζ 0.67 at 3B, 1.0 at 6B in clay (cap not in firm contact) and 8B in sand, linear between; the group the lesser of Σ ζ Qult and the equivalent pier
sources.piles.drilledShaft.punchingSpan: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.6.14 Eq 6.3.50 (p. 777). Note: the print reads qE = (H Br / 10)(qUP - qLo) <= qUP, which is not dimensionless and drops qLo; the engine uses qE = qLo + H/(10 B) (qUP - qLo) <= qUP (B the equivalent shaft's width), the form of its source
sources.piles.settlement.axialShare: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.5 Eqs 6.3.35a-b (pp. 766-767): Sax = (Qp + a Qs) L / (A Ep), a 0.5 clay and silt, 0.67 sand
sources.piles.settlement.cp: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Eq 6.3.35c and Table 6.3.13 (p. 767). Eq 6.3.36 (p. 768) cites 'Table 6.3.9' for Cp, an evident misprint for Table 6.3.13
sources.piles.settlement.csSlope: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Eq 6.3.36 (p. 768): Ssf = Cs Qs / (D qo), Cs = (0.93 + 0.16 L/D) Cp. Cs is used as printed (its source has √(L/D); the printed form is the more conservative). The printed D in the denominator is taken as an evident misprint for the embedded length L (the source form): with D, a typical 14 m pile at a third of its capacity settles over 100 mm by skin friction alone, 35 times the L form, which no load test supports. Owner to confirm; skinDenominator 'diameter' applies the printed form
sources.piles.settlement.groupWidthExponent: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Eqs 6.3.37-6.3.38 (p. 768): Sg = St (B/D)^0.5 and Rs = n^0.5; the larger is taken
sources.piles.settlement.blockDepth: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.5, long term settlement for pile group (p. 769): a solid foundation at 2/3 of the pile length
sources.piles.settlement.modulus: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Eqs 6.3.40-6.3.41 and Table 6.3.14 (pp. 769-770); the lower M of each range is used. Eq 6.3.40 prints ln((σ1'/σ0')^j), which is zero for j = 0; read as the j = 0 form S = H/M ln(σ1'/σ0'), and Eq 6.3.41 as the j > 0 form S = H/(M j) [(σ1'/σr)^j - (σ0'/σr)^j] (2H/M for j = 0.5). For a clay with j > 0 the larger of the two is taken
sources.piles.settlement.limits: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.5 (p. 766) refers to the shallow foundations' limits as 'Table 6.3.7', an evident misprint for Table 6.3.8 (Table 6.3.7 is the presumptive bearing values); Table 6.3.8 is used
sources.piles.detailing.bored: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Secs 3.10.4.1-3.10.4.2 and 3.10.4.9 (pp. 761-766): f'c >= 21 MPa, shafts in 50 mm steps from 400 mm; fy >= 420 MPa, longitudinal steel >= 0.5 % of Ac for Ac <= 0.5 m2, 0.375 % for 0.5-1 m2, 0.25 % above, bars >= 16 mm for diameters >= 600 mm, at least 6 bars, hoops not closer than 100 mm, cover >= 75 mm, cement 350 kg/m3 dry and 400 kg/m3 submerged, w/c 0.45, Table 6.3.12 mixes (pp. 765-766)
sources.piles.detailing.bored.guidance: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.3.11 (p. 764): build-ability guidance for piles in compression only, fy 420 MPa, reinforced at least 3 m below the cut-off (note c)
sources.piles.detailing.bored.casingExtra: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.4.9 (p. 763): reinforce compression piles 2 m below the temporary casing; Table 6.3.11 note (c) (p. 764) prints 1 m. The more conservative 2 m is used
sources.piles.detailing.driven: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.1.31 (pp. 756-757): service stress <= 0.33 f'c; not a long column where cu > 10 kPa; L/B <= 50; longitudinal steel 1 % for L < 30B, 1.5 % for 30-40B, 2 % above 40B; ties >= 6 mm, >= 0.4 % of the gross volume over 3B at each end and 0.2 % in the body; f'c >= 21 MPa, 28 MPa for hard driving (driving stress > 1000 kPa)
sources.piles.detailing.driven.impact: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.3.2 (p. 760): handling stresses with the pile's weight plus 50 % for impact. The clause is printed for prestressed piles; it is the code's only handling impact allowance and is applied to precast piles too (formerly cited as ACI 543R)
sources.piles.detailing.castInPlace: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Secs 3.10.2.2, 3.10.2.3 and 3.10.2.7 (p. 758): butt area >= 650 cm2, tip diameter >= 200 mm; Sec 3.10.2.3: portions not laterally supported designed as columns, bars 3000 mm below that plane; Sec 3.10.2.7: clear cover >= 50 mm, 75 mm in corrosive or marine environments or concrete placed by water or slurry displacement
sources.piles.detailing.drilledShaftBarsBelow: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.6.21 (p. 781): unsupported portions of drilled shafts designed as columns, bars at least 5 m below the plane of adequate lateral restraint
sources.piles.detailing.corrosiveCover: SAEngine practice, not BNBC (after BNBC 2020 Part 6 Secs 3.10.1.29 and 3.10.2.7, pp. 754-758): Sec 3.10.1.29(b) asks for minimum cover of concrete piles on a corrosive site (Sec 3.10.1.29(a): chloride >= 500 ppm, sulphate >= 2000 ppm or pH < 6) without a value; the 75 mm of Sec 3.10.2.7 is applied to every concrete pile there
sources.piles.detailing.concrete: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.6.1 and Table 6.3.5 (p. 715): Table 6.3.5 prints 18 MPa for cast-in-situ piles against 21 MPa in Sec 3.10.4.1, and 25 MPa for driven piles against 21 MPa in Sec 3.10.1.31: the larger of each pair is the least f'c checked
sources.piles.lateral.allowableDeflection: SAEngine practice, not BNBC: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.1.21 (p. 752) asks the least of soil failure, structure and head deflection, and Sec 3.10.6.15 (p. 779) leaves the tolerable movement to the designer; without the pile type's own limit, the head deflection of the analysis is held to the 5 mm of the load-test criterion (ii) of Sec 3.10.1.21
sources.piles.lateral.groupRatio: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.6.15 and Table 6.3.16 (p. 778): shafts act individually at c/c > 2.5B normal to the load and > 8B parallel to it; in-line ratios 1.00 at 8B, 0.70 at 6B, 0.40 at 4B, 0.25 at 3B (interpolated; 0.25 below 3B)
sources.piles.lateral.unbracedCu: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Secs 3.10.1.21 and 3.10.1.31 (pp. 752, 756): piles standing unbraced in air, water or soils not capable of lateral support designed as columns; Sec 3.10.1.31 (p. 756): fully embedded piles are not long columns where cu > 10 kPa
sources.piles.loadTests.compression: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Secs 3.10.1.17 and 3.11.1-3.11.2.1 (pp. 749, 789-794): Sec 3.10.1.17: test pile to 2 x the design load, working pile 1.5 x; safe load of a single pile the lesser of 2/3 of the load at 12 mm and 1/2 of the load at 10 % of D (7.5 % of the bulb of under-reamed piles); of a group, the load at 25 mm and 2/3 of the load at 40 mm. Sec 3.11.2 (p. 791): at least 2 % of the piles tested, at least one bored pile per project, not earlier than 4 weeks. Sec 3.11.2.1 (pp. 793-794): Davisson offset 0.15 in + D/120 (driven precast piles), BS 8004 10 % of D (allowable 50 % of it), IS 2911 (10 % of D or 12 mm; allowable 2/3 at 12 mm, 1/2 at 10 % D), Butler-Hoy (tangent at 1.27 mm/ton), Brinch Hansen 90 %; ultimate / FS 2.0-2.5 where failure occurs (2.0, Sec 3.10.1.18). Sec 3.11.1 (p. 789): integrity tests on 100 % of the piles. Sec 3.11.2.1 refers working-pile tests to 'Sec 3.10.1.16', an evident misprint for Sec 3.10.1.17
sources.piles.loadTests.compression.butlerHoyTon: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.11.2.1(f) (p. 794) prints 1.27 mm/ton without saying which ton; the metric tonne (9.81 kN: the smaller slope per kN, so the earlier and lower failure load) is taken as the conservative reading
sources.piles.loadTests.uplift: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.11.3 (pp. 796-797): ultimate from a test / FS 2.0 (1.5 by test, 2.0 by analysis where the uplift is due to wind or earthquake); safe load the lesser of 2/3 of the load at 12 mm and 1/2 of the load at the clear break; initial test to 2 x the design load, routine tests to 1.5 x or 12 mm
sources.piles.loadTests.lateral: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.10.1.21 (p. 752) and Sec 3.11.4 (p. 797): tests to at least 2 x the design load; allowable lateral load the lesser of 1/2 of the load at 12 mm head movement and the load at 5 mm total displacement. Sec 3.11.4 cites 'Sec 3.10.1.20', an evident misprint for Sec 3.10.1.21
sources.piles.downdrag: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Secs 3.10.1.22-3.10.1.23 (pp. 752-753) and 3.10.6.17-3.10.6.19 (p. 780): downdrag of piles in compressible fill or soft soil by a load-transfer analysis to the neutral point, the full ground movement assumed, as part of the design load; swelling uplift resisted below the zone of moisture change. Soft clay by Sec 3.5.8 (pp. 713-714)
sources.piles.downdrag.dragloadFactor: SAEngine practice, not BNBC: BNBC gives no load factor on the dragload; 1.25 (the downdrag factor of the α method in AASHTO LRFD Table 3.4.1-2) is used in the strength check of the section
sources.machine.impactRatio: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.1 (p. 807): impact neglected except on loose granular soil, cranes, heavy machinery, moving equipment, or live load causing impact over 50% of the dead load
sources.machine.speedClasses: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.2 (p. 809): low speed under 300 rpm, medium 300-1000 rpm, high over 1000 rpm
sources.machine.frequencyRatioBelow: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.2 (p. 809): low speed machines, natural frequency at least twice the operating frequency, ratio less than 0.5
sources.machine.frequencyRatioAbove: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.2 (p. 809): high speed machines, natural frequency at most half the operating value, ratio at least 2; amplitude at resonance while starting and stopping
sources.machine.amplitudes: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.2 (p. 810), when the manufacturer gives none: under 500 rpm 0.25 mm; 500-1500 rpm 0.4-0.6 mm horizontal, 0.7-0.9 mm vertical; up to 3000 rpm 0.2 mm horizontal, 0.5 mm vertical
sources.machine.hammerAmplitude: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.2 (p. 810): hammer foundations 10 mm
sources.machine.staticPressure: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.3(ii) (p. 810): 80% of the allowable pressure for static loading
sources.machine.eccentricity: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.2 (p. 810) and 3.20.2.3(v) (p. 811): eccentricity at most 5%
sources.machine.waterDepth: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.3(ix) (p. 811): ground water at least one fourth of the foundation width below the base
sources.machine.method: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.3-3.20.2.4 (pp. 810-811): lumped parameter method, single degree of freedom
sources.machine.participatingMass: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.5 Eq 6.3.51 (p. 812): m = mf + ms, ms between zero and mf
sources.machine.barkanPoisson: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Eq 6.3.53 (p. 813) prints 1 - μ; Barkan's relation has 1 - μ²: both enveloped (owner decision 1)
sources.machine.decrement: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.5 Eq 6.3.58 (p. 814): the exact inverse of δ = 2πD/√(1 - D²), smaller than δ/2π (owner decision 1)
sources.machine.hysteresisDivisor: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.5 Eq 6.3.59 (p. 814) prints D = ΔW/W; the loss per cycle of a viscous system gives ΔW/(4π W), the smaller and conservative D (owner decision 1)
sources.machine.damping: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.5 (p. 814): D of most soils 0.01-0.1
sources.machine.separation: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.3(vi) (p. 811): taken lower than the foundations of adjacent buildings and properly separated
sources.machine.vibration: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.20.2.3(vii)-(viii) (p. 811): vibrations neither annoying nor detrimental to other structures; the limit charts of Fig 6.3.5 as a guide
sources.strutAndTie.tieArm: SAEngine practice, not BNBC: the tie's lever arm of the deep members' own models, 0.9 d
sources.strutAndTie.betaCCC: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.5.2.1 (part 2 p. 495): nodal zones bounded by struts or bearing areas, βn = 1.0
sources.strutAndTie.betaCCT: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.5.2.2 (part 2 p. 495): nodal zones anchoring one tie, βn = 0.80
sources.strutAndTie.betaCTT: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.5.2.3 (part 2 p. 495): the clause prints 'βn = 0.80, βn = 0.60' with its subject missing; its clarification gives it to C-T-T and T-T-T nodes (anchoring two or more ties): the conservative 0.60 is used
sources.strutAndTie.betaPrism: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.3.2.1 (part 2 p. 489): a strut of uniform cross-section, βs = 1.0
sources.strutAndTie.betaBottle: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.3.2.2(a) (part 2 p. 489): bottle-shaped strut with the reinforcement of Sec I.3.3, βs = 0.75
sources.strutAndTie.betaBottlePlain: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.3.2.2(b) (part 2 p. 489): bottle-shaped strut without it, βs = 0.60 λ (λ of Sec 6.1.8.1)
sources.strutAndTie.minAngle: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.2.5 (part 2 p. 488): the angle between any strut and any tie entering a node not less than 25 degrees
sources.strutAndTie.webRatio: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.3.3.1, Eq 6.I.4 (part 2 p. 491): Σ Asi sin αi / (bs si) ≥ 0.003
sources.strutAndTie.general: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 6.1.4.4 (p. 892) and Appendix I Sec I.2.1 (part 2 p. 486): any structural concrete member or D-region may be designed as an idealised truss
sources.strutAndTie.effective: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Eqs 6.I.3 and 6.I.8 (part 2 pp. 489, 494): fce = 0.85 βs f'c in a strut, 0.85 βn f'c in a nodal zone; a strut's fce the smaller of the two (Sec I.3.1, p. 488)
sources.strutAndTie.betaTension: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.3.2.3 (part 2 p. 489): struts in tension members or the tension flanges of members, βs = 0.40
sources.strutAndTie.betaOther: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.3.2.4 (part 2 p. 490): all other struts, βs = 0.60 λ
sources.strutAndTie.lightweightBottle: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.3.2.2(b) (part 2 p. 489): 0.60 λ
sources.strutAndTie.webRatioFcMax: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.3.3.1 (part 2 p. 491): Eq 6.I.4 for f'c not exceeding 40 MPa
sources.strutAndTie.webAngleMin: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.3.3.2 (part 2 p. 491): reinforcement in one direction only at not less than 40 degrees to the strut
sources.strutAndTie.spreadSlope: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.3.3 (part 2 p. 490): the strut's force may be taken to spread at 2 longitudinal to 1 transverse
sources.strutAndTie.deltaFpBonded: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.4.1, Eq 6.I.6 (part 2 p. 492): Fnt = Ats fy + Atp (fse + Δfp), fse + Δfp ≤ fpy; Δfp = 420 MPa bonded
sources.strutAndTie.deltaFpUnbonded: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.4.1 (part 2 p. 492): Δfp = 70 MPa unbonded
sources.strutAndTie.dRegionDepth: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.1 (part 2 p. 481): a D-region lies within h of a force or geometric discontinuity
sources.strutAndTie.compressionSteel: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.3.5, Eq 6.I.5 (part 2 p. 491): Fns = fce Acs + As' fs', fs' = fy for Grade 40 or 60 bars
sources.strutAndTie.nodeArea: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Sec I.5.1, Eq 6.I.7 (part 2 p. 494): Fnn = fce Anz
sources.strutAndTie.equilibrium: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Secs I.2.1-I.2.2 and I.2.6, Eq 6.I.1 (part 2 pp. 486-488): the truss in equilibrium with the factored loads, φ Fn ≥ Fu, Fu the largest of all load cases
sources.strutAndTie.anchorage: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Appendix I Secs I.4.3.1-I.4.3.3 (part 2 p. 493): the tie force developed where its bar centroid leaves the extended nodal zone

bearingCombinations.name: D + L
bearingCombinations.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.9.2(a)(i), Full Dead Load + Normal Live Load (p. 727)

bearingCombinations.name: D + L + E
bearingCombinations.note: E (Sec 2.5.13, strength level) at 1.0 as printed, with the 33% increase of Sec 3.9.3.2; the general allowable stress combinations of Sec 2.7.2 take 0.7E

bearingCombinations.name: 0.9D + B
bearingCombinations.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.9.2(a)(iii), 0.9 x (Full Dead Load) + Buoyancy Pressure (p. 727)

stabilityCombinations.name: D + W
stabilityCombinations.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.14: stability provided by the dead load of the building (p. 800)

stabilityCombinations.name: D + E
stabilityCombinations.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.14 (p. 800); E at 1.0 as in Sec 3.9.2(a)(ii)

granular.name: D + L
granular.note: the sustained combination; (ii) with W or E is transient

cohesive.name: D + 0.5L
cohesive.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 3.9.2(b) CLAY and Sec 3.9.4.4 (pp. 727, 731)

Sand (other than fine sand), gravelly sand, silty sand; dry
